current.text: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.

master.text: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.

predecessors.text: Verify that all input (HTML form fields, REST requests, URL parameters, HTTP headers, cookies, batch files, RSS feeds, etc) is validated using positive validation (allow lists). ([C5](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

Verify that structured data is strongly typed and validated against a defined schema including allowed characters, length and pattern (e.g. credit card numbers, e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, or validating that two related fields are reasonable, such as checking that suburb and zip/postcode match). ([C5](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))
Verify the application has business logic limits or validation to protect against likely business risks or threats, identified using threat modeling or similar methodologies.
Verify that JSON schema validation is in place and verified before accepting input.
Verify that XSD schema validation takes place to ensure a properly formed XML document, followed by validation of each input field before any processing of that data takes place.

summaries.body:
ASVS 5.0.0 V2.2.1 is a merge of several 4.0.3 controls: V5.1.3 (positive/allow-list validation of all input), V5.1.4 (strongly typed structured data against a schema, including related-field reasonableness), V11.1.5 (business-logic limits from threat modeling), plus coverage of JSON schema (V13.2.2) and XSD/XML field validation (V13.3.1). The current clause asks that input be validated against business or functional expectations, using allow lists, patterns, and ranges or an expected structure and logical limits, with an L1 versus L2 scope distinction.

The official mapping disagrees with git: predecessor text is dissimilar and ID-slot lineage diverges. Events on V2.2.1 itself are Authentication-chapter CWE and L1-rebalance work. Mapping and the listed 4.0.3 predecessors are the reliable origin; the git timeline is noisy.

Relative to 4.0.3, the 5.0 wording drops the enumerated input sources (HTML forms, REST, headers, cookies, batch files, RSS) and the separate JSON/XSD schema checks, and instead states a single positive-validation or structure-and-limits rule with L1 limited to input used for business or security decisions. V5.1.4's related-field example (suburb and zip) was split out of this ID; V11.1.5's threat-modeling language is not in the current sentence.

On the predecessor IDs, vanderaj's 2019-01-01 malicious-code refactor touched V13.3.1, kisasondi updated V13.2.2 on 2019-02-13, and work swapped V13.3 and V13.4 for issue #516. Authentication and CWSS events on the V2.2.1 slot are not this control's wording history.
